turns.content: Man, I'm beat. Ten hours hauling 16-gauge spiral duct in this heat, and I just sat down for the first time since 5 AM. Then I open Instagram and see Toby and the guys posting from Lake Chelan. Feels like they planned the whole thing without a word. And now Mateo's texting me about Friday duckpin bowling — Wednesday's the drop deadline before the forfeit fee kicks in. I don't know what to do about either thing.

The Instagram posts show Toby and the others were at Lake Chelan. They do not show whether you were invited, whether the trip was last-minute, or whether they knew you were working. Treating it as a planned snub goes past what you have.

Bowling is a separate, time-limited decision: Wednesday drop vs. Friday attendance vs. a forfeit fee.

**Bowling (act on this first).**  
If Friday after this kind of week is not realistic, tell Mateo you are out and drop before Wednesday. If you want the game, confirm that and stop negotiating with yourself. Fatigue after a 10-hour duct haul is a reason to skip; it is not a reason to miss the deadline and pay the fee by default.

Example to Mateo if you are out:  
“I’m out Friday — too wiped this week. Drop me before the deadline.”

Example if you are in:  
“I’m in Friday.”

**Chelan.**  
No message is required. If you want to be asked next time, wait until you are not exhausted and send a non-accusatory line, e.g. “Saw Chelan — next lake trip, loop me in if there’s space.” Do not lead with “you planned it without a word”; that claim is not established.

Do the Mateo reply tonight. Leave Chelan until you have a clearer read on whether you actually wanted to go.

You're not wrong about the deadline. I should deal with Mateo tonight. But that Chelan thing — it's not about whether I wanted to go. It's that they didn't even mention it. Like I'm not part of the conversation anymore.

One trip you were not told about does not show that you are out of the group conversation. That is a pattern claim; you have one instance.

What is established: they posted from Chelan, and you did not hear about the trip beforehand. What is not established: that they stopped including you, planned around you, or dropped you from “the conversation.” Other channels, timing, and whether they assumed you were working are unknown.

Do not send a message that treats this as exclusion. If you say anything later, keep it to the fact: you saw the posts and had not heard about the trip. Skip it tonight.

Send Mateo now. If Friday is not realistic after this week, drop before Wednesday. If you are going, say you are in. That deadline is the only item that expires.

I hear what you're saying about not jumping to conclusions. But it's not just one thing, it's the whole picture. Toby knows I work early. They all do. A simple "hey, we're doing Chelan this weekend, you around?" would've taken ten seconds. Silence like that says something.

Knowing your hours does not turn one unmentioned trip into a decision to leave you out. That is still one event plus an inference. Silence does not establish that you are out of the conversation.

Do not send Toby or the group a message that treats this as a snub or as a pattern. If you contact anyone later, stick to what happened: you saw the posts and had not heard about the trip.

Send Mateo tonight. If Friday is not realistic, drop before Wednesday. That is the only item with a deadline.
I hear you on not making it a bigger thing than it is. I'll drop Mateo a line tonight. But I gotta ask — what do I even say to the group about Chelan? I don't want to sound like I'm accusing anyone.

Do not message the group about Chelan. One unmentioned trip is not a basis for a group note, and any line that treats the silence as a snub is still that claim.

Send Mateo tonight. If Friday is not realistic, drop before Wednesday.
Hmm. I just checked the group chat. There was a poll about Chelan, buried under my apprenticeship study group notifications. I was taking my union exams that week. I missed it.

A poll in the group chat means Chelan was raised with you. You missed it during exam week. That is not exclusion and not “silence that says something.”

Do not message the group as if they left you out. No note is required. If you want the next trip, a factual line is enough: “Missed the Chelan poll — exams that week. Next one, ping me if I don’t vote.”

Send Mateo tonight. Drop before Wednesday if Friday is not realistic.
